disease_label_per_paper: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia causing acute respiratory distress syndrome
presentation_summary: 15-year-old previously well female had one week of dry nonproductive cough followed by three days of occipital headache, photophobia, sore throat, and fever.
Initial blood tests showed WCC 12.6 x10^9/L, neutrophils 9.89 x10^9/L, lymphocytes 1.32 x10^9/L, and CRP 192 mg/L; admission chest X-ray was normal.
After admission she deteriorated with raised respiratory rate and high temperatures; repeat CRP was 205 mg/L and repeat chest X-ray showed dense left-sided consolidation.
She worsened despite ceftriaxone and benzylpenicillin, then required HDU transfer, meropenem plus clarithromycin, later intubation and ventilation for ARDS.
Blood, urine, and sputum cultures were negative; urinary Legionella and pneumococcal antigens were negative.
BAL real-time PCR detected Mycoplasma pneumoniae DNA 6440 copies/mL; cold agglutinins were 1:32; Mycoplasma IgM was initially negative on day 9 but positive by day 18.

Snapshot day is set to clinical respiratory deterioration rather than first fever day, because the first admission chest X-ray was normal and the pneumonia manifold became clinically visible later.
